mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen in each of the last four weekly means (-20.7 to -14.0), showing commuters are re-entering the transport network; because transit trips are complements to discretionary errands, the same reopening impulse lifts retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises further over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean in any window where TRANSIT rose for four consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS collapsed to -27.0 at t-1w then rebounded to -17.1 at t-0w, a snap-back in outdoor leisure demand; when the park series crosses back above -20, discretionary out-of-home trips are resuming and the retail corridor adjacent to that leisure activity gains footfall within two weeks.

failure_condition: In instances where PARKS crosses above -20 from below -25, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed the prior 14-day mean.

failure_condition: In weeks where GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +25, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is equal to or higher than its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES remains deeply negative at -9.6, meaning a large share of office workers are still away from central business districts; weekday lunchtime and after-work retail demand is therefore structurally suppressed, and while WORKPLACES stays below -8 that drag keeps RETAIL_REC from rising in the very near term.

failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES is below -8, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days exceeds its prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The monotone decline in RESIDENTIAL from +10.9 to +7.3 is an always-on relaxation signal: each weekly reduction in stay-at-home time releases household hours into out-of-home categories, and the released hours are disproportionately spent in retail and recreation rather than in transit-only trips.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days falls below its prior 14-day mean while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline week-on-week.

regime_hint: spring outdoor season under partial reopening

mechanism_narrative: Under an easing-restrictions policy regime, TRANSIT recovery (-20.7 to -14.0) leads the release of retail capacity because transport reopening precedes venue-capacity easing; the lag structure means RETAIL_REC catches up to transit over roughly four weeks, giving a positive four-week change.

failure_condition: In an easing-restrictions regime where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve over four weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the preceding 28 days.
